$comment: A role a body steps into: a character is a role plus a disposition, and the two kinds of body that step in are kept categorically apart — a person is a real human being; a session character is a role a language model steps into. Characters and personnel are disjoint rosters, and that is a categorical claim, not a style preference: recording a session character as personnel would let a record blur the one distinction the whole roster is built to hold. Hardened from the record, not invented: the emsenn character record (lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/board-of-directors/services/executive-office/lib/characters/emsenn/emsenn.md, 'A real human being, not a session character... that distinction is the most load-bearing one in the record'), the 561-group glossary's disjoint-rosters rule, the characterizing carrier's 'a role plus a chi-nucleus disposition', and the quiescent personae (first-officer, chief-engineer, diviner) that proved the form.

name.$comment: What the character is called, as it is said: 'Morgan "emsenn" Sennhauser', 'Cassia Lorne'.

kind.$comment: The most load-bearing distinction in the roster: a person is a real human being; a session character is a role a language model steps into. Nothing downstream may blur these.

disposition.$comment: The chi-nucleus disposition: how this character characteristically moves — the settled tendency a stranger could recognize across sessions. A role with no disposition is a costume, not a character.

$comment-absences: No holds-offices key: incumbency is the double settlement of recognition and induction, recorded as an incumbency record, and a character that could assert its offices would assert a readout — the office schema refuses a holder key for the same reason, and the seat belongs to neither party's self-record. No model key: which model animates a session character belongs to the act of animating, never to the role. No personnel fields: persons are recorded on the personnel roster; this record is the role, even when a person holds it.
